content.text:
Some of factorio's settings are not stored in any config file on this server — they are read from the environment when the game starts, and the only place an instance can set them is .grizzly/env, at the top of the data directory. It is always there, often empty. Don't go looking for a config file for these: there isn't one, and searching for it is time spent on something that cannot be found.

Exactly these settings do anything in that file, and the rest are ignored: LOAD_LATEST_SAVE and SAVE_NAME. A line naming anything else is dropped when the game launches, so the change will look like it worked and won't have.

Read the file first to see what's already set, then change it like any other config file — one setting at a time — and restart to apply it. That restart self-guards: if the game refuses a value and won't start, the previous version of the file is restored and the server restarted automatically, and you'll be told. So a value you're unsure of is worth trying rather than talking around; afterwards, read_logs to confirm it took rather than assuming.

There is no supported way to install mods on factorio through this bot — no registry is wired up for it, so there is nothing to search and nothing to write. Say so plainly. Don't improvise an install by hand through the file tools: anything put there that way is outside everything that would otherwise check it and put it back. If someone wants mods on this game, escalate it as a feature request.

Yes, it can. Factorio has a server setting called `auto_pause` that pauses the game whenever nobody is connected. It's turned on for your server, which is why the factory stops when the last person leaves. Turning it off (`"auto_pause": false` in `config/server-settings.json`) and restarting will keep the factory running with nobody on.

I couldn't make that change, though. I can see the line `"auto_pause": true,` in the file, but my edit tool says it can't find that text. I tried twice and got the same error, and my file reader can't reach the server either. I didn't want to overwrite the whole settings file without being able to check what I'd be replacing, so I've passed this to a human. They'll make the change and restart the server. Your world and all your other settings are untouched.
input.reason: User wants the Factorio server to keep running when empty, so auto_pause needs to go from true to false in /factorio/config/server-settings.json, followed by a restart. run_shell (cat) shows the file is 765 bytes and contains the line `  "auto_pause": true,` exactly once. edit_file on config/server-settings.json failed twice with "not found": once with old_text `"auto_pause": true,` and once with the full line including its indent and newline. read_file on the same path returns "couldn't reach" even though about_server says Ready and run_shell works. That suggests the file tools are seeing a different path or view than the shell does. There's also a 3714-byte config/server-settings.json.grizzly.bak, so something has rewritten this file before. I didn't use write_file blind. Needed: set auto_pause to false (leave auto_pause_when_players_connect as false), restart, and check the logs to confirm the server no longer pauses when empty. Also worth looking at why edit_file/read_file can't see this path.
